paragraphs.title: God’s Kingship and the Foundation of the World

answers: To the people of the earth
To the LORD
To the waters
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.”
easy.q: To whom do the earth, the world, and those who dwell in them belong?

answers: Upon the mountains
Upon the gates
Upon the seas
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “For he hath founded it upon the seas.”
easy.q: Upon what did the LORD found the earth?

answers: The LORD
The inhabitants of the earth
The rivers
easy.explanation: The verse attributes both founding and establishing the earth to the LORD.
easy.q: Who founded and established the earth?

answers: The second verse explains how the LORD founded the earth
The second verse describes the inhabitants of the earth
The second verse calls for the gates to open
medium.explanation: First, the psalm declares that everything belongs to the LORD; then it describes how He founded and established the earth.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the first two verses?

answers: The gates of the sanctuary
The inhabited earth
The streams beneath the earth
medium.explanation: In this verse, “the world” refers to the earth and all that dwells in it.
medium.q: What does “the world” refer to in verse 1?

answers: The LORD only observes the earth
The earth belongs only to its inhabitants
The LORD is the source of the earth’s foundation and stability
medium.explanation: The two actions describe the LORD establishing the earth and setting it firmly in place.
medium.q: What can be understood from the fact that the LORD both founded and established the earth?

answers: The LORD’s rule extends over the whole world and all its inhabitants
Only the waters belong to the LORD
Only the sanctuary belongs to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The verse places the earth, the world, and everyone dwelling in them under the LORD’s ownership.
challenge.q: What central idea follows from mentioning the earth, the world, and their inhabitants together?

answers: First the gates, and then the earth
First the earth’s belonging to the LORD, and then His founding of it
First mankind, and then mankind’s blessing
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from declaring that the world belongs to the LORD to describing His work in founding the earth.
challenge.q: What is the order of thought in verses 1–2?

answers: “clean hands”
“the King of glory”
“upon the seas ... upon the floods”
challenge.explanation: This phrase identifies the waters upon which the LORD founded and established the earth.
challenge.q: Which phrase refers both to the seas and to the waters on which the earth was established?

paragraphs.title: Those Worthy to Ascend to the Sanctuary

answers: “Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD?”
“Who is this King of glory?”
“Who shall dwell upon the earth?”
easy.explanation: Verse 3 begins with the question, “Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD?”
easy.q: What question is asked about ascending the LORD’s hill?

answers: A person with great physical strength
A person standing near the gates
A person with clean hands and a pure heart
easy.explanation: Verse 4 answers, “He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart.”
easy.q: What kind of person is described as worthy to ascend the LORD’s hill?

answers: Gates and rivers
Blessing and righteousness
Earth and seas
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness.”
easy.q: What does the worthy person receive from the LORD?

answers: They describe clean actions, a pure heart, and truthful speech
They describe strength in battle
They describe ownership of the earth
medium.explanation: The verse speaks of clean hands, a pure heart, refusing vanity, and not swearing deceitfully.
medium.q: How do the requirements in verse 4 relate to being worthy to enter the holy place?

answers: A strong body
An inward life that is clean and sincere
Great wealth
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a person whose inner character is pure.
medium.q: What does “a pure heart” mean in verse 4?

answers: The person becomes the King of glory
The person receives blessing and righteousness
The person establishes the earth
medium.explanation: After describing the worthy person, the psalm says that he receives blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the person’s upright character and the result described?

answers: Strength, victory, and authority
Clean conduct, a pure heart, and truthful living without deceit
Wealth, wisdom, and long life
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes clean hands, a pure heart, honest speech, and freedom from deceit.
challenge.q: What complete set of qualities is required of the worthy person?

answers: Those who seek the LORD and seek His face
Those who dwell upon the seas
The ancient gates
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 explains that this generation consists of those who seek the LORD and seek His face.
challenge.q: To whom does “This is the generation of them that seek him” refer?

answers: The question concerns entrance, and the answer describes the person’s character
The question concerns the earth, and the answer concerns the seas
The question concerns warfare, and the answer concerns the gates
challenge.explanation: The psalm first asks who may enter the holy place, then explains the moral qualities of that person.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the question in verses 3 and the answer in verse 4?

paragraphs.title: The Entrance of the King of Glory

answers: To the rivers
To the gates and everlasting doors
To the inhabitants of the earth
easy.explanation: Verses 7 and 9 say, “Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors.”
easy.q: To whom is the command given to lift up their heads for the entrance of the King of glory?

answers: Jacob
The inhabitants of the earth
The LORD
easy.explanation: The passage identifies the King of glory as the LORD, including the LORD of hosts.
easy.q: Who is the King of glory?

answers: Strong and mighty, mighty in battle
With clean hands and a pure heart
Dwelling upon the rivers
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 8?

answers: The gates are called to lift up their heads for the LORD’s entrance
The earth is described as founded upon the waters
The person’s heart is described
medium.explanation: After verses 3–6, the psalm calls upon the gates to rise for the entrance of the King of glory.
medium.q: What happens after the description of those worthy to enter the holy place?

answers: Powerful
Pure
Seeking
medium.explanation: The word describes the LORD as possessing great strength and power.
medium.q: What does “strong” mean in the description of the LORD in verse 8?

answers: To emphasize preparation for the entrance of the King of glory
To describe how the earth was founded
To introduce those who seek the LORD
medium.explanation: The repetition heightens the emphasis on opening and lifting up the gates for the LORD’s entrance.
medium.q: Why is the command to the gates repeated in verses 7 and 9?

answers: “them that seek him”
“The LORD strong and mighty”
“a pure heart”
challenge.explanation: This phrase presents the LORD as strong, mighty, and victorious in battle.
challenge.q: Which phrase emphasizes that the LORD possesses power and victory?

answers: It emphasizes the LORD as ruler over all forces
It describes the morally pure person
It explains how the earth was founded
challenge.explanation: The title presents the LORD as the commander and ruler of all hosts and powers.
challenge.q: What does the title “the LORD of hosts” add to the description of the King of glory?

answers: The gates are called to lift up their heads, the King of glory is questioned, and He is identified as the LORD
The earth is founded, the person receives righteousness, and the gates are shut
The seeker asks for the LORD’s face, and then the waters establish the earth
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the command to the gates, to the question about the King of glory, and finally to the answer identifying Him as the LORD.
